question.problem: Find the formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence if the $1$st term is $0$ and the $9$th term is $40.$
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the $n$th term is given by 

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d.
$$

We already know that the first term is ${a}_{1}=0,$ so we just need to figure out the common difference $d.$ 

To find the common difference, we can find the total difference between the terms ${a}_{1}=0$ and ${a}_{9}=40$ and divide it by the number of jumps, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{9}-{a}_{1}}{9-1} \\  & =\frac{40-0}{9-1} \\  & =\frac{40}{8} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

So the formula for the $n$th term of this arithmetic sequence is  

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =0+(n-1)(5) \\  & =5n-5.\end{aligned}
$$
